brief: Last array entry that passes a test
description: Call predicate for each entry of array, from the last to the first, until it returns true, then return that entry, as ECMAScript findLast does. Entries whose value is undefined are included. Only the indexes there at the start are visited, each as it is when it is reached; an index predicate removed reads as undefined, as in ECMAScript. If no entry passes, the result is undefined (the same as a found undefined entry; use find_last_index if you need to tell those apart).

parameters.description: The array to walk. A string is not walked as an array: write [...value] to walk its characters.
parameters.name: array

parameters.dataTypeParameter: (value: any, index?: integer, array?: array) => boolean
parameters.description: Returns true for the entry to return. A script function is called with (value, index, array); a built-in function is called with the value alone, since its other parameters have their own meanings.
parameters.name: predicate

returns.description: The last matching entry, or undefined if none match.
